parts.name: Multiple-choice cloze
parts.instr: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.example: 0 — A familiar  B known  C usual  D normal → A
parts.title: City foxes
paras: Urban foxes have become a (0) familiar sight in many British cities. Although plenty of people enjoy spotting them in the street at night, others [[1]] them as pests that [[2]] through rubbish bins and dig up carefully planted flowerbeds.

Foxes first moved into towns in the 1930s, [[3]] advantage of the new suburban gardens, which offered both food and shelter. Today, it is [[4]] that there are around 150,000 foxes living in urban areas across the country.

Contrary to popular [[5]], foxes rarely attack cats or dogs, and they generally [[6]] away from people whenever they can. Scientists who have [[7]] foxes with tiny tracking collars have also discovered that a single animal can cover a surprisingly large [[8]] in just one night.

q.expl: Устойчивая конструкция: regard sb/sth as sth — считать кем-то/чем-то. После believe/suppose нужно that или to be, а count в значении «считать» звучит как count them among.
rummage through — рыться в чём-то (в мусоре, в сумке). Seek не употребляется с through, а explore и inspect не передают смысл «копаться в поисках еды».
Коллокация take advantage of — воспользоваться. С make/get/have слово advantage в этом значении не сочетается.
It is estimated that… — по оценкам… Точно сосчитать всех лис нельзя, поэтому counted не подходит; measured — про размеры, valued — про ценность.
Фиксированное выражение contrary to popular belief — вопреки распространённому мнению. Другие слова в этой фразе не используются.
keep away from — держаться подальше от. С away и from из этих глаголов сочетается только keep.
fit sb/sth with sth — оснастить чем-то (fitted with collars). Put и placed требуют on (put collars on foxes), dressed — про одежду.
cover a distance — преодолеть расстояние. Length и width — размеры предмета, а не путь, который проходит животное.

parts.name: Open cloze
parts.instr: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: Learning to juggle
paras: Juggling is one of (0) the oldest forms of entertainment in the world. Most people assume it is a skill you are either born with [[9]] without, but in fact almost anyone can learn it. All you need [[10]] three soft balls and a little patience.

Start [[11]] throwing a single ball from one hand to the other, making sure it rises [[12]] higher than eye level. [[13]] you can do this comfortably, add a second ball. The trick is to throw the second one just as the first reaches the top of its path.

Don't worry if you keep dropping them – everybody does at first. [[14]] really matters is practising a little every day rather than [[15]] hours at a time. Researchers have even found that learning to juggle changes the structure of the brain, [[16]] suggests it is good exercise for the mind as well as the hands.

q.expl: Пара either … or: either born with or without.
All you need is… — всё, что нужно, это… После All глагол в единственном числе.
start by doing sth — начать с того, чтобы сделать что-то.
no higher than — не выше, чем. Not higher тоже бывает, но здесь нужно одно слово перед сравнительной степенью: no.
Once = как только. When тоже засчитывается: «когда сможешь, добавь второй мяч».
What really matters is… — что действительно важно, так это… What здесь значит «то, что».
Параллель: practising a little every day rather than (practising) for hours at a time.
, which относится ко всей предыдущей части предложения. That после запятой не ставится.

parts.name: Word formation
parts.instr: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of some of the lines to form a word that fits in the gap in the same line. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: The power of sleep
paras: Most of us spend (0) roughly a third of our lives asleep, yet [[17]] are only beginning to understand why sleep is so important. While we sleep, the brain sorts through the day's experiences and stores the most [[18]] information.

A lack of sleep, on the other hand, can lead to poor [[19]] and even affect our [[20]] to make sensible decisions. Teenagers are often [[21]] to go to bed early, partly because of the [[22]] of their phones.

Experts recommend switching off screens an hour before bed, since the [[23]] of the light tricks the brain into thinking it is still daytime. [[24]], even small changes to your routine can make a real difference.

q.expl: Нужно существительное-деятель во множественном числе (are): scientists.
Прилагательное перед information: useful — полезная. Usable (пригодный к использованию) не передаёт смысл.
После прилагательного poor нужно существительное: concentration.
После our — существительное: ability to do sth — способность что-то делать.
Смысл отрицательный (подросткам не хочется ложиться рано): unwilling to do sth. Не забывай про приставку — частая ловушка Part 3.
После the и перед of нужно существительное: attraction — притяжение, соблазн.
the ___ of the light → существительное brightness — яркость.
Наречие-связка в начале предложения: Fortunately. Смысл позитивный, поэтому не unfortunately.

parts.name: Key word transformation
parts.instr: For questions 25–30, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between two and five words, including the word given.
parts.example: 0 What type of music do you like best? FAVOURITE → What IS YOUR FAVOURITE type of music?

q.first: It was such a boring film that I fell asleep.
q.expl: such + a + adj + noun ⇄ so + adj: such a boring film → the film was so boring (that).

q.first: I haven't been to the cinema for two months.
q.after: to the cinema was two months ago.
q.expl: haven't done for… ⇄ the last time I did … was … ago. Обрати внимание: Past Simple (went).

q.first: Lucy regrets not studying harder for the test.
q.expl: Сожаление о прошлом: wish + Past Perfect — wishes she had studied.

q.first: They will deliver the new sofa on Friday.
q.expl: Пассив в будущем: will be + V3 — will be delivered.

q.first: It wasn't necessary for us to bring food.
q.expl: didn't need to do — не было необходимости. needn't have done — сделали, хотя было не нужно. Оба варианта засчитываются.

q.first: Tom started learning the guitar three years ago.
q.expl: started … ago ⇄ has been doing … for — Present Perfect Continuous.

parts.name: Multiple choice
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a teenage beekeeper. For questions 31–36, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which you think fits best according to the text.
parts.title: Up on the roof
parts.subtitle: Kate Dalton meets sixteen-year-old beekeeper Sam Okafor
paras: When Sam Okafor suggests we meet ‘at work’, I assume he means a café, or perhaps the supermarket where so many teenagers earn their pocket money. Instead, I find myself climbing four flights of stairs in a block of flats in south London and stepping out onto a flat roof, where six white wooden boxes stand in a neat row against the low wall. The sound reaches me before anything else: a deep, steady hum, like a fridge that never switches off. ‘Don’t wave your arms about,’ Sam says calmly, handing me a veil. ‘They don’t mind visitors. They just don’t like drama.’

Sam was twelve when a neighbour, a retired bus driver called Mr Ellis, asked if he would help carry a hive up to the roof. ‘I only said yes because it meant I could get out of doing my homework,’ he admits with a grin. But something about the insects caught his attention. Mr Ellis, whose knees were no longer up to the stairs, began to rely on him more and more, and by the following spring Sam was doing most of the work himself, with his neighbour shouting instructions up the stairwell.

It hasn’t always been easy. In his second year, a cold, wet summer meant the bees could barely leave the hives, and two colonies didn’t survive the winter. ‘I took it personally,’ Sam says. ‘I kept going over everything I’d done, looking for the mistake.’ It was Mr Ellis who pointed out that even experienced beekeepers lose colonies, and that the weather is not something anyone controls. ‘He said bees teach you patience whether you want to learn it or not. At the time I thought that was just the kind of thing old people say. Now I think he was right.’

These days the hives produce around eighty jars of honey a year, which Sam sells to neighbours and a local bakery. He is careful not to exaggerate the business side of things. ‘People hear “sixteen-year-old with his own company” and imagine I’m rich,’ he laughs. ‘After I’ve paid for jars, labels and equipment, I make about enough to buy a new pair of trainers.’ What he values far more, he says, is the way the honey has brought the building together. Residents who had lived on the same corridor for years without speaking now stop him on the stairs to ask how ‘their’ bees are doing.

Sam is planning to study biology at university, though he isn’t sure he wants to become a scientist. ‘Maybe I’ll be the person who explains science to everyone else,’ he says. Before I leave, he lifts a frame out of a hive to show me thousands of bees crawling over the comb, perfectly unbothered by us. I realise I have stopped worrying about being stung. Sam, I notice, isn’t wearing gloves. ‘You get to know when they’re in a good mood,’ he says, as if this were the most obvious thing in the world.

q.stem: What does the writer suggest about her expectations in the first paragraph?
opts: She had been told exactly where the meeting would be.
She thought Sam probably had an ordinary part-time job.
She was nervous about having to climb onto a roof.
She had heard about the noise the bees make.
q.hl: I assume he means a café, or perhaps the supermarket where so many teenagers earn their pocket money
q.expl: Она думала, что «at work» — это кафе или супермаркет, где подрабатывают подростки, то есть обычная подработка. Где будет встреча, ей заранее не сказали — место её удивило. Про страх перед крышей и про шум пчёл до приезда в тексте ничего нет: гудение она услышала уже на месте.

q.stem: Why did Sam first agree to help Mr Ellis?
opts: He had always been fascinated by insects.
He was worried about his neighbour’s health.
He hoped to earn some extra money.
He saw it as a way of avoiding schoolwork.
q.hl: I only said yes because it meant I could get out of doing my homework
q.expl: «get out of doing my homework» = отвертеться от домашки. Ловушка — вариант про здоровье соседа: колени Mr Ellis упомянуты, но это причина, почему сосед позже стал полагаться на Сэма, а не почему Сэм согласился.

q.stem: How did Sam react when two colonies died?
opts: He blamed Mr Ellis for giving him poor advice.
He was certain the weather was the only cause.
He assumed at first that he had done something wrong.
He decided to stop keeping bees for a while.
q.hl: I kept going over everything I’d done, looking for the mistake
q.expl: «took it personally», «looking for the mistake» — он искал свою ошибку. Мысль, что виновата погода, — это слова Mr Ellis, а не реакция Сэма в тот момент.

q.stem: What does ‘that’ refer to in the third paragraph (‘I thought that was just the kind of thing old people say’)?
opts: the claim that bees teach you patience
the idea that nobody can control the weather
the fact that experienced beekeepers lose colonies
the suggestion that Sam should check his work
q.hl: He said bees teach you patience whether you want to learn it or not
q.expl: Вопрос на референцию: смотри на предложение прямо перед that — «bees teach you patience». Именно это казалось Сэму «стариковской фразой».

q.stem: According to Sam, the most rewarding thing about selling honey is
opts: the money he has managed to save.
the interest shown by local businesses.
the way it has connected people in his building.
the experience of running his own company.
q.hl: What he values far more, he says, is the way the honey has brought the building together
q.expl: «values far more … brought the building together» — главное для него, что соседи стали общаться. Вариант про деньги опровергается: заработка хватает только на кроссовки.

q.stem: What impression does the writer give of Sam in the final paragraph?
opts: He takes unnecessary risks to impress visitors.
He is completely at ease with his bees.
He is uncertain whether to carry on beekeeping.
He wishes more people understood science.
q.hl: Sam, I notice, isn’t wearing gloves. ‘You get to know when they’re in a good mood,’
q.expl: Без перчаток, спокойно объясняет, «as if this were the most obvious thing» — ему совершенно комфортно с пчёлами. Ловушка — вариант про науку: он хочет объяснять науку, но не жалуется, что её не понимают.

parts.name: Gapped text
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a woman who rowed across the Atlantic. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37–42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
parts.title: Alone on the ocean
parts.subtitle: Mia Hartley spent 74 days rowing across the Atlantic by herself. She tells us what it was really like.
paras: People often ask me why I wanted to row across an ocean, and I’ve never found a short answer. I’d done some rowing at university, but nothing on this scale. [[37]] Once the idea was in my head, it simply wouldn’t go away.

Preparing took nearly two years. Apart from training in the gym six days a week, I had to learn how to repair a water-maker, navigate by the stars and treat my own injuries. [[38]] In the end, a local engineering company agreed to cover most of the costs in exchange for having its name painted on the side of the boat.

The first week was the worst. The waves were bigger than anything I had trained for, and I was seasick almost all the time. [[39]] I’d row for two hours, sleep for two hours, and repeat, day and night.

People imagine that the loneliness must have been unbearable, but I rarely felt alone. Dolphins would swim alongside the boat for hours, and once a whale surfaced so close that I could smell its breath. [[40]] Hearing my sister describe what she’d had for dinner was surprisingly comforting.

There were frightening moments, of course. About halfway across, a storm turned the boat over three times in a single night. [[41]] When I finally climbed out at dawn, half my food supply had been washed away.

Arriving in Antigua was strange. After weeks of silence, the noise of the harbour was almost too much, and my legs had forgotten how to walk on solid ground. [[42]] Ask me again in a year, though, and I might give you a different answer.

sents.A: Then, one evening, I watched a documentary about a man who had crossed the Pacific in a tiny boat.
sents.B: Finding the money was, if anything, even harder.
sents.C: Things only improved once I had settled into a routine.
sents.D: I also had a satellite phone, which meant I could call home once a week.
sents.E: Each time, I was strapped inside the tiny cabin, unable to do anything but wait for it to roll back up.
sents.F: For now, I have no plans to do anything like it ever again.
sents.G: My trainer insisted that I should practise in winter conditions first.

q.expl: После gap: «Once the idea was in my head» — значит, в пропуске должно появиться, откуда взялась идея: документальный фильм (A).

Абзац перечисляет трудности подготовки (Apart from training…), затем «In the end, a company agreed to cover the costs». Мостик — про деньги: «Finding the money was even harder» (B). G не связана с costs.
Сначала «первая неделя была худшей», после пропуска описан режим: «row for two hours, sleep for two hours». Связка — «стало лучше, когда я вошла в routine» (C).
После пропуска: «Hearing my sister…» — нужно объяснить, как она слышала сестру: спутниковый телефон (D). Also указывает на добавление к дельфинам и киту.
«turned the boat over three times» → «Each time, I was strapped inside…» (E). После: «When I finally climbed out» — она была внутри каюты.
«For now, I have no plans…» связано с «Ask me again in a year, though… a different answer» (F). Though показывает контраст с «сейчас».

parts.name: Multiple matching
parts.instr: You are going to read an article in which four young people describe their first summer job. For questions 43–52, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.
parts.title: My first summer job

texts.name: Daniel
texts.body: I spent last July working at a campsite in the south of France. I’d seen the advert pinned up on the noticeboard outside the languages office at school and applied almost as a joke. My French was reasonable on paper, but the first few days were painful: I’d rehearse a sentence in my head, get it wrong anyway and go bright red while the guests waited politely. Luckily, the other staff were brilliant. Two of the lifeguards started correcting me over lunch, and by the end of the month I was even dealing with the occasional complaint about noisy neighbours without panicking. I’d tell anyone to do something that scares them a bit.

texts.name: Priya
texts.body: Everyone assumed I had it easy working in my aunt’s café, but it was the opposite. She expected more from me than from anyone else on the staff and wouldn’t let me get away with anything – if I was five minutes late, I heard about it all day. The early starts were tough too: we opened at seven, so I was up before six. What I did enjoy was being trusted with the till by the end of the summer. I put almost everything I earned aside, because I’d set my heart on a new laptop for school, and I managed to buy it in September with a bit left over.

texts.name: Jake
texts.body: I didn’t want a job with fixed hours because I train with my football club four evenings a week, so I decided to start my own dog-walking business. I printed some leaflets and pushed them through every door on our estate, and within a fortnight I had six regular customers. Walking several dogs at once takes more organisation than you’d think – you have to plan routes so the ones that don’t get on are never together. The worst moment was when a terrier slipped its lead in the park and disappeared. I spent forty minutes searching, heart pounding, before I found it sitting outside the café.

texts.name: Emma
texts.body: I worked as an assistant at a summer sports camp for eight- to twelve-year-olds. It was exhausting – by the end of each day I could barely keep my eyes open – and, to be honest, the pay was a lot lower than I’d been led to believe at the interview. But I didn’t really care, because I loved it. Watching a shy kid finally score a goal or swim a width of the pool was the best feeling. Until then, I’d always assumed I’d study law like my mum, but the camp made me realise that teaching is what I really want to do.

q.stem: being treated more strictly because of a family connection?
q.hl: She expected more from me than from anyone else on the staff
q.expl: Тётя требовала с неё больше, чем с остальных: «expected more from me than from anyone else».

q.stem: discovering which career they would like to follow?
q.hl: the camp made me realise that teaching is what I really want to do
q.expl: «made me realise that teaching is what I really want to do». Ловушка: «study law like my mum» — это прежний план.

q.hl: a terrier slipped its lead in the park and disappeared
q.expl: Собака убежала, он искал её 40 минут «heart pounding».

q.stem: choosing work that fitted around another commitment?
q.hl: I didn’t want a job with fixed hours because I train with my football club
q.expl: Тренировки по футболу 4 раза в неделю — поэтому работа без фиксированных часов.

q.hl: get it wrong anyway and go bright red while the guests waited politely
q.expl: «go bright red» = покраснеть от смущения. Ловушка: Emma «exhausting» — это усталость, а не смущение.

q.hl: the other staff were brilliant. Two of the lifeguards started correcting me
q.expl: Коллеги-спасатели поправляли его французский за обедом.

q.stem: being paid less than they had expected?
q.hl: the pay was a lot lower than I’d been led to believe at the interview
q.expl: Зарплата оказалась ниже, чем обещали на собеседовании.

q.stem: saving up for a particular purchase?
q.hl: I put almost everything I earned aside, because I’d set my heart on a new laptop
q.expl: «put aside» = откладывать, цель — ноутбук.

q.stem: how they found out about the job?
q.hl: I’d seen the advert pinned up on the noticeboard
q.expl: Объявление на доске у кабинета языков. Ловушка: C печатал листовки — это реклама его услуг, а не поиск работы.

q.hl: I printed some leaflets and pushed them through every door on our estate
q.expl: Листовки в каждый почтовый ящик — реклама собственного бизнеса.
